key_insight: Microscopic impurities nucleate perovskite degradation, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can flag these harmful defects within seconds.
engineering_relevance: Rapid, non-invasive impurity screening could support stability-focused quality control for scalable perovskite solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation onset.
Detect and quantify impurities with reflected-light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation initiating at impurity–perovskite interfaces, while higher impurity density correlated with faster early degradation.
watch_item: The abstract does not report detection accuracy or validation across manufacturing conditions, leaving deployment robustness uncertain.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
